explanation: Flood-fill from every boundary white cell, marking reached cells T so they are visited once. A white cell is enclosed exactly when no such path reaches it. Restore T to W and turn all other cells black.
timeComplexity: O(rows × columns) Every cell is marked once and generates at most four neighbor attempts.
spaceComplexity: O(rows × columns) The queue and, in C#/JavaScript, visited bitmap can hold O(rows×columns) entries.

correctness: The BFS marks exactly the white cells connected by white steps to a boundary: boundary white cells initialize it and each expansion follows an allowed adjacency. Thus unmarked white cells, and only those cells, are enclosed. Recoloring that complement preserves every boundary-connected region.
walkthrough: On ["BBBW","BWBW","BBBW"], the rightmost white column touches the boundary and remains white. The lone interior white cell is surrounded by black and becomes black, giving ["BBBW","BBBW","BBBW"]. The native callable mutates the matrix and returns void/None; expected is the matrix observed by the wrapper.
edgeCases: Only horizontal and vertical adjacency counts.
Empty dimensions are unchanged; T is an internal marker and is not an input color.
